title: Olivia and the Garden Beds
subtitle: Dirt under the fingernails.
blurb: Olivia waters the wooden raised beds beside the white house — lettuce, pots, a chicken coop, and a green can that makes the plants drink.

magic.home: The plants drank. Olivia did too — a glass of water, after.

pages.heading: The wooden beds
pages.text: {Olivia} stood by the wooden {garden} beds. Leaves were already busy being green. "Thirsty?" she asked them, as if leaves could answer.

pages.heading: The green can
pages.text: The green watering {can:can/pour} was heavier than it looked. {Olivia:olivia/ask} tipped it. A silver ribbon of water landed on the dirt. The dirt went dark and glad.

pages.heading: Little pots
pages.text: Colored pots sat on the gravel like a tiny town. {Olivia} gave each one a sip. "Fair is fair," she said. Even the smallest pot got a drink.

pages.heading: The wire house
pages.text: A little wire house stood in the gravel. Something rustled. {Olivia} whispered, "We are growing lunch. You can watch." The rustle said, all right.

pages.heading: The white house watches
pages.text: The white {home} with the dark roof watched the garden the way a kind giant watches. {Olivia:olivia/wave} waved at the windows. The windows shone back.

pages.heading: Dirt under the nails
pages.text: The {can:can/pour} was empty. {Olivia}'s fingernails had a line of dirt, like a badge. The leaves looked taller. Maybe they were. Maybe she was.

end.heading: The End
end.text: You {read} the whole {story}. Gardens drink. Then they grow. That is the deal.
end.prompt: If you had a watering can, what would you grow first?
